user.title: Add LinqAura
user.description: Connect your LinqAura switches through your LinqAura account, or connect one switch directly on your home network.

cloud.title: Sign in to LinqAura
cloud.description: Sign in with the e-mail and password you use in the LinqAura app. Home Assistant keeps only a sign-in token, never your password, and gets every switch on the account with live updates.

data_description.email: The e-mail address of your LinqAura account.
data_description.password: The password of your LinqAura account.

local.title: Connect a switch directly
local.description: Enter the address of a LinqAura switch on your home network. Switches are usually found by themselves and show up under Discovered.

data_description.host: The switch's IP address or host name on your home network.

discovered.title: LinqAura switch found
discovered.description: How should Home Assistant connect to {name}?

menu_option_descriptions.local_key: Home Assistant controls the switch on your home network, also when the internet is down. It reads the switch's key from your LinqAura account once.
menu_option_descriptions.cloud: Home Assistant signs in to your LinqAura account and gets every switch on it, with live updates. Needs internet.

sign_in.title: Get the switch's key
sign_in.description: To connect {name} directly, Home Assistant reads the switch's local key from your LinqAura account once. Sign in with the account the switch is on (as owner or shared with you). The sign-in ends right away; nothing but the key is kept.

data_description.email: The e-mail address of your LinqAura account.
data_description.password: The password of your LinqAura account.

reauth_confirm.title: Get the switch's new key
reauth_confirm.description: {name} no longer accepts the key Home Assistant has. This happens when someone loses access to the switch and the cloud makes a new key. Continue to read the new key from your LinqAura account.

data_description.host: The switch's IP address or host name on your home network.

error.too_many_attempts: Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
error.not_linqaura: That address doesn't answer like a LinqAura switch.
error.setup_mode: The switch is in setup mode. Add it in the LinqAura app first, then try again.
error.not_on_account: This switch isn't on that LinqAura account. Sign in with the account it was added to, or one it is shared with.

abort.not_supported: This device isn't a supported LinqAura switch.
abort.setup_mode: The switch is in setup mode. Add it in the LinqAura app first.
abort.no_local_key: This switch has no local key yet. Update its firmware and make sure it has been online once, then try again.
abort.key_refused: The switch didn't accept the key from your account. Make sure it is online so it gets its current key from the cloud, then try again.
abort.locked_out: The switch is refusing connections for a while after wrong attempts. Try again later.
abort.wrong_account: That is a different LinqAura account. Sign in with the account this entry belongs to.
abort.wrong_switch: A different switch answers at that address.
abort.already_in_cloud: This switch is already in Home Assistant through your LinqAura account (cloud).

local_key_refused.message: The switch no longer accepts Home Assistant's key.

locked_out.message: The switch refuses connections for a while after wrong attempts.

setup_mode.message: The switch is in setup mode.

command_failed.message: The command didn't reach the switch: {error}
